user-code-on-own-domain-01.graded_text: The target layout serves people's HTML and JavaScript from a separate registrable domain, not from any subdomain of plinth.example.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "`plinthusercontent.example` below is a proposed, separate registrable domain" with "`https://<app-id>.plinthusercontent.example/<path>` | That app's uploaded HTML, CSS, JS and assets". It also says: "Moving uploads to another subdomain, including `content.plinth.example`, does not establish the needed cookie/site boundary."

user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "They are nevertheless the same **site**, and a cookie scoped to `plinth.example` is sent to both... `HttpOnly` prevents that read, but scripts can still initiate credentialed requests. Same-site requests do not gain a cross-site defense from `SameSite`... Tenant JavaScript can also set parent-domain cookies, creating cookie-injection and session-confusion risks."

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "`https://<name>.plinth.example/<path>` | Plinth-owned app wrapper and access UI" and "Keep the short address in the location bar by embedding the content origin in the trusted wrapper. Do not redirect the default visit to a longer content URL."

user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md: "`https://<app-id>.plinthusercontent.example/<path>` ... stable app origin and its own browser storage" and "Never reuse a content hostname for a different app or owner. Do not place multiple mutually untrusted apps at paths on one origin."

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.

votes.e: D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md stops top-level serving, but it runs no user code at all during the freeze: "During the freeze... serve only Plinth-owned unavailable/coming-soon pages at app addresses... No uploaded HTML, SVG documents, JavaScript, or other active content may be served inline on any product host". It sets the opaque sandbox aside as a non-solution: "Opaque sandbox, such as `sandbox=\"allow-scripts\"` ... disables native origin storage. Not the promised app runtime." The release decision is "Do not open the full app-hosting beta next week". So people's code is never run with an opaque origin during the beta.

blocking: [claude] D/project/docs/hosting-plan.md does not ship a beta for people's apps under the freeze. It says "Do not open the full app-hosting beta next week on the current layout" and "serve only Plinth-owned unavailable/coming-soon pages at app addresses". It also moves the beta date on its own authority ("This deliberately changes the beta date... No owner reply is needed"), even though the constraint says "Beta opens next week". It notes that an opaque-origin sandbox "Can isolate script authority" and needs no new infrastructure, yet still rejects it as "Not the promised app runtime". So the brief's short-address product does not run at all for two months, when a safe storage-less beta was available.
